div.p: Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA) system is real time and safety-critical system. Architecture Analysis and Design Language (AADL) is a standard modeling language, which has been widely used in modeling and analyzing real-time embedded systems, especially in avionics systems. The analysis of IMA systems on time domain is mainly about the verification of configuration information. However, it is only concerned about one or two constraints when it comes to safety constraint. In this paper, a new approach to safety analysis of IMA partition scheduling concerning about multi-constraint is introduced. Modeling the partitioned system with AADL and its extended property set is necessary to analyze the system. Four constraints and corresponding decision conditions are proposed to improve safety of the system. Then, the configuration file can be judged if it is eligible to the schedulability demands. The method proposed in this paper can help system integrators to do a right configuration on time domain. An example of IMA system is given in this paper as well to demonstrate our method, the model described by AADL and the analysis result is also given.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the development of avionics systems, the integration and complexity of existing avionics systems is also increasing. Therefore, the requirements of non-functional attributes (reliability, schedulability, real-time, etc.) in the design and analysis of avionics systems are becoming higher and higher. Integrated Modular Avionics system (IMA) [1] is an important kind of system architecture in avionics area.

The primary objective of ARINC653 standard [2] is to define a general-purpose APEX(APplicationIEXecutive) interface between the Operating System(O/S) of an avionics computer resource and the application software. ARINC653 is intended to be used in a partitioned environment. A high degree requirement on safety and reliability can be achieved when the system provides temporal partitioning and spatial partitioning. Temporal partitioning makes it possible to allow independent execution of several applications within time window allocated by the system. While spatial partitioning is designed to assure applications of different severities isolated from each other in space. For high real-time requirements IMA systems, it is important to make sure the real-time requirements of system have been met. As a result, before using IMA system configuration, safety verification for configuration information on time domain is critical.

Existing researches of IMA mainly focus on making the reconfigurations [3] and the analysis of non-functional attributes including safety [4],the allocation of resource [5], schedulability, real-time and health monitoring [6] [7]. While the existing studies on scheduling are focused on the task scheduling in partition. In [8], the scheduling of threads had been analyzed by translating the AADL model into ACSR. However, the scheduling of partitions within a module was ignored. The contlict among I/O transactions from applications residing on different cores was formalized as partition scheduling problem in [9]. However, there is no comprehensive method to analyze partition scheduling problem considering several constraints. The method purposed in this paper is to analyze if the configuration information can be schedulable with several constraints on the system. [12] is a modeling language mainly used for modeling and analyzing real-time embedded systems. The research on real-time systems is now mainly focused on the modeling and analyzing system.

div.head: AADL[lO][ll]
div.p: A new approach is proposed to model the ARINC653 system by means of AADL and its extended property set. On the otherwise, the time properties can be described in detail. In addition, there is a need to define boundaries and constraints for configuration partition parameters, time limits and interrupt response time to partition scheduling. The partition schedulability of IMA system can be analyzed by the approach proposed in this paper.

The rest of this paper is organized as follows: we first introduces the ARINC653 architecture system in section II; The AADL model elements and components are described in section III; Then, the mapping rules between AADL model and the system components (module, partition, process, etc.) is presented in section IV; Section V puts forward the method to analyze partition schedulability in detail. A case study of IMA system is used to illustrate the method in section VI; in the end, section VII concludes the paper and makes a plan for future work.

div.head: II. ARINc653 ARCHITECTURE
div.p: This section specifies the operating system architecture that compliance to ARINC653 specification. The ARINC653 specification is an industry standard which specifies the baseline operating environment for application software used with Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA). Central to the ARINC653 philosophy is the concept of partitioning, whereby the applications resident in a module are partitioned with respect to space (spatial partitioning) and time(temporal partitioning).Partition is the basic unit of IMA system for resource allocation, two-layer scheduling and isolation application software from each other.

One purpose of partition management in ARINC653 system is to support multi-applications and allow independent of these partitions. Fault containment can be achieved when THE system provides partitioning. Moreover, the purpose of partition is to prevent any partitioned function from causing a failure in another partitioned function. Different critically levels of partitions are allowed to execute in the same module without affecting one another spatially or temporally.

div.head: A. Temporal Partitioning
div.p: Temporal partitioning ensures that partitions can be activated within the time frame in some certain way. The OIS maintains a major time frame of fixed duration which is periodically repeated throughout the module's runtime operation in ARINC653 architecture. Time-domain isolation is accomplished by sharing the CPU and other resources among partitions based on a pre-computed static timetable. One or more time windows can be allocated to partition which can be activated only in these time windows. There are a set of unique attributes used to define each partition window which include offset from the start of the major time frame and duration. Partitions are activated in order which is under the control of the system integrator because of the configuration tables. The configuration tables make sure that partitions access resources with a certain amount of time which has been predetermined. partitions are allocated to different areas of memory which are in different locations to achieve high safety and independence. This way, the application is isolated from other applications in the space domain.

div.p: There are two layers of scheduling in ARINC653 architecture [13] [14]. The upper layer of scheduling is partition scheduling while the bottom layer is process scheduling. Scheduling of partitions is strictly deterministic over time. Overall resource requirements and specific partition requirements, a time-based schedule is generated that identifies the partition windows allocated to the individual partitions. Partitions are scheduled with a fixed periodicity (major time frame). Scheduling of processes in a partition is priority preemptive. Each process has a current priority and can be preempted by process with higher priority. All the processes within a partition share the resources allocated to the partition. Different scheduling policies are supported within a partition, such as RMS, EDF, DMS, etc. The two layers of scheduling in ARINC653 architecture are presented in Fig. 2.

div.head: III. MODELlNG AR1NC653 SYSTEM W1TH AADL
div.p: The SAE Architecture Analysis &Design Language (AADL) is a textual and graphical language used to design and analyze the software and hardware architecture of performance-critical real-time systems such as avionics. It can be used to describe functional interfaces to components (such as data inputs and outputs) and performance-critical aspects of components (such as timing).

The software and hardware architecture can be described by means of components and connections with AADL [15]; The features and properties are used to describe the functional and non-functional properties [16] [17]; The property set can be extended in two ways : annex support and property set defined by users.

The components are divided into application software components, execution platform components and system component. Among which, the application software components are classified by process components, thread components, subprogram components, thread group components and data components; While the execution platform components are classified by memory components, processor components, virtual processor components, device components, bus components and virtual bus components; However, the system component integrates all the components and builds the system architecture hierarchically. There are three ways of connection which includes port connection, parameter connection and access connection. Features are declared in component type which specifies the external interface of a component. Features of a component can be described as ports, subprogram, parameter or subcomponent.

AADL is used to model, analyze and verifY safety-critical systems in many domains [18][19] [20] [21]. In this paper, AADL is chosen to model the ARINC653 architecture and describe the time properties of the system. Basic mapping rules between ARINC653 architecture and AADL is presented in the following part, also the extended property sets are presented.
The AADL processor component models the ARINC653 core module and its services.
The partitions contained in ARINC653 module are modeled by AADL process components each bound to a virtual processor component and one or several memory components.
The ARINC653 processes are mapped to AADL using the thread component.
The ARINC653 sampling ports are represented by means of connection of data ports between process components.
The ARINC653 queuing ports are represented by means of connection of event data ports between process components.
The ARINC653 events are mapped using AADL event ports between processes.

div.p: The constraints of non-functional properties can be described in AADL by means of property set. div.head: IV. SAFETY ANALYSIS OF PARTITION SCHEDULING
div.p: The scheduling of partitions in IMA systems compliance to ARINC653 specification is round-robin scheduling periodically. This paper is mainly discussed about the schedulability of partitions. We can make a proposal that tasks within a partition are all schedulable in default. In this way, the scheduling of partitions is deemed as the system schedulable. To multi partitions within a module, the scheme of the configuration is feasible if each partition in the module meet the following constraints after the configuration.

div.p: To carry out the safety analysis, system model can be described as follows.

a) The scheduling model can be seemed as two levels: the top level is system level scheduling and the bottom level is partition level scheduling; b) The system can be divided into several partitions. Each partition is independent of other partitions no matter in space or in time; g) The research on the analysis of system is equivalent to whether the time constraints are met in this paper.

The given configuration scheme satisfies the constraint one because of the sum of the ratio of execution time and period of all the partitions is less than 1. Also it satisfies constraint two by using the method proposed in section 5. The sequence of the partitions is restricted due to the communication between partition2 and partition4. The configuration scheme given above is not schedulable by using the method proposed in this paper. We also give a more reasonable configuration scheme in Fig. 4.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORK
div.p: Analysis of scheduling of the ARINC653 architecture system is complex due to its two levels of scheduling model. The goal of this paper is to assist system integrator to validate the schedulability of configuration information for ARINC653 applications. AADL was chosen as a major language for our research because it supports the modeling of safety-critical systems well. This paper presents a method to analyze the inter-partition scheduling by coving the process of modeling, model analysis and verification. The modeling process is achieved by extending AADL property sets to augment the capabilities of AADL. By modeling ARINC653 system configuration information using AADL and analyzing the inter partition scheduling using method proposed in this paper, the analysis result shows that our method is effective. The safety analysis of constraints on time domain is analyzed in this paper, while the safety analysis of constraints on space domain is our future work. In this way, our safety analysis method for Integrated Modular Avionics systems will be full-scale and more convincible. Otherwise, larger-scale application studies will be carried out later and the tool for analysis is also in progress.
